mentl/1167b51:
A node minted after parse carries no span, so 41 of T_EqTypeUnprovable's 56
sites reported at 0:0 with nothing to locate them, which is a count standing
in for a finding. The EmitSite effect carries the emission in flight:
installed per fn record at emit_one_fn_to_string, where the name is already
in hand, defaulting to "module scope" for the fold helpers and table
emissions that genuinely stand outside every record. It retires when a
post-parse node carries its nearest authored span; the comment says so.

Two hypotheses died to the measurement. The eight declarations whose rows the
change widened are all show/fold helper generators, which reads as "the sites
are in generated leaves" — false, an effect row is transitive reachability,
not the firing site. And the class is not handler arms, which is what the
peer entry predicted: the 41 land in 41 ordinary wheel fns, concentrated in
cw_compete_lead (8), cw_compete_trail (6), alpha_pairs_ok (3) and
list_compare_loop (2), with only 2 of the 56 in twin bodies.

The class renames itself by that evidence: a comparison whose operand comes
out of a destructured container the graph never closed. cw_compete_lead
matches leads[k] as a five-tuple and compares each component against a
parameter; the components are vars because the list's element type was never
proven — the family Hβ.infer.record-row-vars-are-not-unioned names one
constructor over. Every one is an Int or a handle at runtime, which is why
the word compare holds and the battery never caught it. So arm-twinning
closes the fixture and the arm class while the bulk is the container element
type, and the base/twin pairs raise the next measurement: whether a floor
body whose every call site redirects to a twin is emitted dead, in which case
its comparison wants deleting rather than proving.

mentl/1168e7e:
The cycle discipline's entry test was a wrong proxy for cyclicity — a
self-recursive singleton is a cycle. Both forms marched: 1,764 movers
with the gate against 930 without, and the wheel emits ~3,700 lines
smaller. The movers line gains its total, and that number turned a
saturated sixteen-slot list into a dig: 930 minimized to a fifteen-line
reproduction of the source, banked RED. A cycle member's row is
published as a value at its own decl exit, before its co-members are
judged, so their effects never reach it — and the member whose
accumulated tail keeps a live co-member edge is the one that stays
correct, which makes the cut the defect, not the openness. Pin
74d63b7c, CLEAN m2 == m3, census 0, frontier 332/0.

mentl/11c1e55:
When a perform site lives in a fn called outside its `~>` chain at
lower-time (e.g., compile_stdin's emit_module performs wat_emit while
the `~> wat_stdout` chain wraps compile_stdin's BODY, not
emit_module's), the lower-stage handler-stack is empty and
$lower_resolve_handler_for_op returned 0 → LConst(0) fallthrough.
Empirically: 7 op-direct calls in m2.wat across the entire wheel.

Substrate move: at HandlerDeclStmt-time register each arm's op_name
→ handler_name in $lower_default_op_handler_map. lower_resolve_
handler_for_op now falls back to the map when the stack walk fails.
The wheel uses each effect with a single default handler; map
lookup returns hname for ops the stack walk couldn't find. Real
Tier 2 evidence-passing per Koka JFP 2022 (closure ev-slot
call_indirect) lands in named follow-up Hβ.lower.tier2-evidence-
passing for multi-handler ambiguity (post-L1).

Empirical: m2.wat 7 → 1028 direct op-calls. wat2wasm clean
(was: undefined-fn errors → 0). Top targets:
  412 op_wat_stdout_wat_emit
   72 op_graph_handler_graph_bind
   54 op_buffer_packer_pack_byte
   44 op_diagnostics_handler_report
   ...

Cascade closures (cleanup):
- emit_handler.wat: starts_with_wasi tightened to exact-match
  against the WASI import set (9 names). Prior loose prefix check
  fired on `wasi_filesystem_*` handler arm names — false positive
